programs.nl_rule:
The input is a 3x3 grid containing grey (X) cells and black (.) cells. The grey cells form a pattern against the black background.

Create an output grid that is exactly twice the size of the input in both dimensions (so a 3x3 input becomes 6x6). Replace each cell in the input with a 2x2 block: each grey (X) cell becomes the 2x2 checkerboard pattern B R / R B (blue top-left, red top-right, red bottom-left, blue bottom-right). Each black (.) cell becomes a 2x2 block of all black (. . / . .).

The input is a 3x3 grid. The output is a 6x6 grid (2x the input dimensions in each direction). The background color is black (.). The output is composed entirely of 2x2 blocks, each corresponding to one cell of the input.

content.text:
Let me plan. The rule: each grey(5) cell becomes 2x2 [[1,2],[2,1]], black becomes 0s. Output is 2x the size.

I should show a demonstration, then probe with a new input, verify student got it, then start exam.

Let me show_example with a different input than the teacher example to be safe. Actually the teacher example is teacher-only, student hasn't seen it. But "near-copy of an input already shown" — I should vary. Let me create a demonstration with a pattern.

Let me use input:
[[5,0,5],
 [0,5,0],
 [5,0,0]]

Output 6x6:
cell(0,0)=5 -> [[1,2],[2,1]]
cell(0,1)=0 -> zeros
cell(0,2)=5 -> [[1,2],[2,1]]
row: [[1,2,0,0,1,2],[2,1,0,0,2,1]]
cell(1,0)=0, cell(1,1)=5, cell(1,2)=0
row: [[0,0,1,2,0,0],[0,0,2,1,0,0]]
cell(2,0)=5, cell(2,1)=0, cell(2,2)=0
row: [[1,2,0,0,0,0],[2,1,0,0,0,0]]

Let me use show_example with this. Then query_student with another input. Actually I could use show_transformed_input too. Let me do a couple demonstrations and one probe.

Plan: 
1. show_example with the above.
2. query_student with a different input.

Let me do the first call.

Let me build the full output.

Input:
1 0 1
0 1 0
1 0 0

where 1 means grey(5).

Output rows:
r0: [1,2,0,0,1,2]
r1: [2,1,0,0,2,1]
r2: [0,0,1,2,0,0]
r3: [0,0,2,1,0,0]
r4: [1,2,0,0,0,0]
r5: [2,1,0,0,0,0]

Good.

Then query_student with input:
[[0,5,0],[5,0,5],[0,5,5]]

gold:
cell(0,0)=0, (0,1)=5, (0,2)=0
row0: [0,0,1,2,0,0]
row1: [0,0,2,1,0,0]
cell(1,0)=5,(1,1)=0,(1,2)=5
row2: [1,2,0,0,1,2]
row3: [2,1,0,0,2,1]
cell(2,0)=0,(2,1)=5,(2,2)=5
row4: [0,0,1,2,1,2]
row5: [0,0,2,1,2,1]

I'll do the query. Since student has seen demonstration, should be fine.

Let me make the two calls sequentially (show_example then query_student). Actually they're independent? The query depends on student having learned from demonstration, but I can call sequentially. Let me do show_example first, then query.

Actually I can do them in the same block? They're independent calls but the query's success depends on learning. Better to do sequential to confirm. But instruction says calls with no dependencies can be batched. Let me just do show_example first.
I'll teach the Student with a demonstration, then probe with a novel input.

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.
